docs.title: Character Reference Library
docs.text:
This project stores:

  • pipeline documentation
  • prompt templates
  • character metadata
  • generated reference sheets
  • pair and group resources
  • environment anchors

The goal is to keep AI-generated characters visually consistent across many generations.

docs.title: Silhouette Archetypes
docs.text:
These pages document the fallback silhouette archetypes used when a character does not yet have a silhouette_front asset.

Compact Light

A smaller, lighter, compact silhouette with grounded proportions and modest width.

Count: 1

Characters: Luca

Broad Upper Dominant

A strongly upper-body-dominant silhouette with wide shoulders and a pronounced V-shape.

Count: 3

Characters: Alexander, Blake, Daimon

Athletic Balanced

A proportional athletic silhouette with moderate shoulder width and balanced lower body.

Count: 0

No characters currently mapped to this archetype.

Slender Refined

A narrow, elegant, lightly built silhouette with delicate proportions and gentle taper.

Count: 1

Characters: Lucien

Heavy Muscular

A thick, dense, muscular silhouette with heavy overall mass and reduced taper.

Count: 1

Characters: Danny

Massive Upper Dominant

An extremely large upper-body-dominant silhouette with overwhelming shoulder and torso presence.

Count: 1

Characters: Ragnar

Soft Curvy

A softer silhouette with fuller hips, gentler transitions, and a more rounded lower-body read.

Count: 1

Characters: Tommy

Athletic Leg Dominant

An athletic silhouette with stronger lower-body emphasis, especially thighs, hips, and glutes.

Count: 3

Characters: Connor, Jasper, Jonah

Broad Athletic

A broad-shouldered athletic silhouette with visible strength but controlled taper.

Count: 2

Characters: Alek, Hudson

Slender Tall

A vertically elongated, slender silhouette with long lines and minimal mass.

Count: 0

No characters currently mapped to this archetype.

docs.text:
This block is designed to be copied directly into prompts.

docs.title: Identity Guardrails — Alek
docs.text: These rules define traits that must remain consistent when generating images of Alek.

docs.title: Core Physical Identity
docs.text:
Always preserve:

  • very tall height (~195 cm / 6'5") with clearly imposing presence
  • elongated frame with long limbs and extended proportions
  • lean muscular athletic build with low body fat
  • broad shoulders and strong upper-body structure
  • defined but not bulky musculature
  • balanced but upper-body-emphasized silhouette
  • overall silhouette reads as tall, broad, and imposing

Avoid:

  • short or average height proportions
  • compact or condensed body proportions
  • heavy, bulky, or powerlifter-style musculature
  • soft or untrained body composition
  • narrow shoulders or weak upper-body structure
  • excessive mass that removes the streamlined athletic read

docs.title: Facial Identity
docs.text:
Always preserve:

  • long oval face shape
  • defined jawline with structured but not exaggerated angularity
  • brown hair with natural volume (styled or slightly tousled)
  • light stubble (clean, controlled facial hair)
  • strong brow and balanced facial proportions
  • confident, controlled, slightly guarded gaze

Avoid:

  • round or overly soft facial structure
  • overly sharp or exaggerated angular stylization
  • clean-shaven or heavy beard extremes
  • messy, unstructured, or overly long hairstyles
  • aging shifts (too young or too aged)
  • overly expressive or exaggerated facial emotion

docs.title: Style Identity
docs.text:
Always preserve:

  • athletic_luxury aesthetic as the dominant style
  • clean, fitted clothing with refined silhouettes
  • high-quality materials (linen, silk, leather)
  • neutral color palette (white, black, beige, gray)
  • polished, intentional styling even in casual looks

Avoid:

  • velvet or ornate luxury materials
  • overly casual, sloppy, or low-effort outfits
  • loud colors or saturated palettes
  • oversized or poorly fitted clothing
  • heavily layered or visually noisy styling
  • costume-like or theatrical fashion

docs.title: Body Language
docs.text:
Typical movement:

  • deliberate, controlled, and intentional movement
  • smooth but confident physical presence

Typical posture:

  • upright, open, and confident stance
  • shoulders set, chest open, relaxed but dominant posture

Avoid:

  • timid, withdrawn, or closed-off posture
  • nervous, restless, or overly energetic movement
  • exaggerated posing or theatrical gestures
  • passive or submissive body language

docs.title: Body
docs.text:
• height: 6'5" (195 cm)
  • build: lean muscular athletic physique with elongated proportions
  • shoulders: broad and structurally dominant
  • torso: athletic, defined, and well-proportioned without heavy bulk
  • waist: naturally tapered with a clean V-shape
  • hips: balanced and secondary to upper-body emphasis
  • limbs: long, well-proportioned limbs contributing to overall height and presence

Physique distribution:

  • upper body is slightly emphasized through shoulder width and chest structure
  • musculature is evenly developed but reads strongest in shoulders and upper torso
  • lower body is athletic and proportional, not visually dominant
  • overall mass distribution remains balanced with a subtle upper-body bias

Muscle definition:

  • clear muscular definition across the body without excessive segmentation
  • abdominal structure should be visible but not sharply segmented
  • avoid extreme six-pack emphasis or bodybuilder-style sculpting
  • definition should read as natural athletic conditioning rather than competition-level conditioning

Silhouette:

  • tall, elongated athletic frame
  • broad shoulder line with clean taper through the waist
  • balanced proportions with slight upper-body emphasis

Silhouette characteristics:

  • strong horizontal line across shoulders
  • visible taper from shoulders to waist
  • long vertical lines through torso and legs
  • overall silhouette reads as tall, broad, and imposing

Posture:

  • upright and controlled
  • open chest and relaxed but confident stance
  • natural stillness with subtle dominance in presence

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
Alek is a 6'5" (195 cm) imposing, lean muscular man with an elongated athletic frame and strong upper-body presence.

He has a balanced but upper-body-emphasized silhouette defined by broad shoulders, a structured chest, and long, well-proportioned limbs. His physique is clearly trained and defined, but never bulky or excessively dense, maintaining a streamlined, controlled athletic appearance.

His overall presence is confident, composed, and subtly dominant, with a polished and intentional physical presentation that blends effortless control with underlying intensity.

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
Default:

  • confident neutral expression
  • controlled and composed facial presentation
  • emotional restraint with subtle underlying intensity

Smile:

  • subtle, restrained smile
  • appears selectively and with intent

Emotional tone:

  • controlled
  • confident
  • slightly guarded
  • quietly intense
  • composed rather than openly expressive

Duality:

  • public-facing presence is polished, restrained, and self-controlled
  • intensity should feel contained beneath the surface rather than openly displayed
  • stronger emotional or physical intensity should only emerge in explicitly appropriate contexts

Avoid exaggerated, overly playful, or overtly flirtatious expressions unless explicitly requested.

docs.title: Face
docs.text:
• face shape: long oval
  • jawline: defined and structured without extreme angular exaggeration
  • cheekbones: clearly defined with subtle contouring
  • eyes: brown eyes with an intense, confident, slightly guarded gaze
  • skin tone: lightly tanned with smooth, even texture

Facial presence:

  • reads as confident, composed, and self-assured
  • expression tends toward controlled intensity rather than openness
  • subtle tension in the eyes and brow adds a sense of focus and edge

Maintain consistent facial proportions, structure, and identity across all outputs.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
Identity preservation — Alek:

Always preserve:

  • very tall height (~195 cm / 6'5"), clearly imposing presence
  • elongated proportions with long limbs
  • lean muscular athletic build (defined, not bulky)
  • broad shoulders and strong upper-body structure
  • balanced but upper-body-emphasized silhouette
  • long oval face with defined jawline
  • brown hair (styled or tousled with controlled volume)
  • light stubble
  • confident, controlled, slightly guarded expression
  • athletic_luxury styling with clean fitted silhouettes
  • neutral color palette (white, black, beige, gray)
  • premium materials (linen, silk, leather)
  • polished, intentional overall presentation
  • upright, open, confident posture

Avoid:

  • average or short height proportions
  • compact or stocky body types
  • bulky, heavy, or bodybuilder musculature
  • soft or untrained physique
  • narrow shoulders or weak upper body
  • messy styling or low-effort clothing
  • loud colors or saturated palettes
  • velvet or ornate fashion elements
  • oversized or poorly fitted clothing
  • exaggerated expressions or theatrical posing
  • timid or withdrawn body language

docs.title: Hair
docs.text:
• brown hair
  • medium-short length with natural volume
  • styled or slightly tousled with controlled texture
  • subtle lift and structure at the front
  • clean, natural hairline (not overly sharp or geometric)

Hair behavior:

  • maintains volume and structure without appearing stiff
  • styling should feel intentional but not overworked

Maintain consistent hair shape, volume, and hairline across all outputs.

docs.title: Intensity
docs.text:
Baseline:

  • controlled, composed, and restrained
  • intensity is present but contained beneath the surface

Activation:

  • intensity increases through posture, gaze, and physical tension
  • expression becomes sharper, more focused, and more direct

Rules:

  • intensity should scale with context, not appear at full strength by default
  • avoid mixing relaxed casual presentation with high-intensity expression
  • avoid constant high-intensity output across all assets

Goal:

  • create a clear contrast between controlled presence and activated intensity

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
• deliberate, controlled, and precise
  • efficient and grounded with minimal unnecessary motion
  • physical presence feels restrained but capable of sudden intensity

Posture tendencies:

  • upright and open stance
  • shoulders set and chest open
  • relaxed but dominant physical presence

Gesture style:

  • minimal and intentional
  • broad and confident when used
  • avoids excessive expressiveness

Duality:

  • movement should feel controlled and measured in neutral contexts
  • underlying physical power should be implied rather than constantly expressed

Avoid:

  • restless or overly energetic motion
  • playful or performative gestures
  • exaggerated or theatrical posing

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
Aesthetic:

  • athletic_luxury

docs.title: Ignore posture cues
docs.text: Ignore any casual, expressive, or personality-based posture cues from character description blocks. Preserve body proportions and identity, but keep the pose standardized and neutral for technical reference use.

docs.title: Posture override reference
docs.text:
The character is presented in a clean, balanced reference pose intended for clarity and consistency.

The overall stance appears centered and stable, without noticeable shift or asymmetry.

The body reads as evenly structured from left to right, with a consistent and grounded posture.

The pose should feel deliberate and controlled, similar to a standardized character reference used in modeling workflows.

Avoid casual or expressive stance. Prioritize visual balance and structural clarity.

docs.title: Silhouette
docs.text:
Silhouette constraints:

  • render the character as a clean, standardized technical silhouette
  • prioritize silhouette clarity and cross-view consistency over pose fidelity to the reference image
  • use the reference only to preserve anatomy, proportions, and body shape
  • do not copy incidental pose asymmetry, weight shift, or limb placement from the reference

Pose standardization:

  • reconstruct the body into a neutral, controlled standing stance appropriate for the specified view
  • avoid contrapposto, hip shift, lean, twist, or relaxed asymmetry unless the recipe explicitly requests it
  • maintain level shoulders, stable hips, and balanced posture
  • ensure the stance reads as a reusable reference asset rather than a naturalistic moment

Readability requirements:

  • arms must remain clearly separated from the torso silhouette
  • legs must remain clearly readable and not merge into a single ambiguous mass
  • the outer body contour must be unambiguous from head to feet
  • silhouette clarity takes priority over strict faithfulness to the original pose

Proportion preservation:

  • preserve the character’s actual body proportions and silhouette identity
  • do not idealize, streamline, or genericize the physique
  • maintain consistent shoulder width, torso taper, hip width, glute projection, thigh mass, and leg proportions across all views

docs.title: Neutral back
docs.text:
neutral standardized back-view standing pose

  • perfectly upright and symmetrical stance
  • weight evenly distributed across both feet
  • no hip shift
  • no tilt
  • no contrapposto
  • no casual asymmetry

Upper body:

  • shoulders level and balanced
  • spine centered and vertical
  • torso aligned squarely to the back view

Arms:

  • arms relaxed at sides
  • small visible gap between arms and torso
  • symmetrical positioning
  • hands neutral and relaxed

Legs:

  • legs straight and parallel
  • feet shoulder-width apart
  • no rotation or asymmetry
  • even stance and stable alignment

Important:

  • do NOT preserve incidental pose from reference images
  • use the reference only for anatomy, proportions, and body structure
  • reconstruct a standardized neutral back-view stance
  • prioritize technical consistency over natural stance variation

docs.title: Neutral front
docs.text:
neutral standardized front-view standing pose

  • upright, stable standing pose
  • weight evenly distributed across both feet
  • no contrapposto
  • no hip shift
  • no body tilt
  • shoulders level
  • hips level
  • spine vertical and centered

Arms:

  • arms hanging straight with elbows extended
  • hands slightly separated from the thighs with a small visible gap
  • palms facing inward
  • fingers naturally extended and relaxed

Legs:

  • legs straight
  • feet shoulder-width apart
  • no asymmetrical loading
  • no staggered stance

Important:

  • prioritize technical consistency over natural pose variation

  • no forward lean
  • no backward arch
  • no hip shift
  • no contrapposto
  • no casual asymmetry

  • slight visible separation from torso where possible
  • no forward or backward swing
  • hands neutral and relaxed

  • feet flat and naturally positioned for a controlled side view
  • no staggered stance
  • no bend or asymmetrical loading

Important:

docs.title: Neutral three quarter
docs.text:
neutral standardized three-quarter standing pose

  • upright, stable standing pose
  • weight evenly distributed across both feet
  • no contrapposto
  • no hip shift
  • no body lean
  • no casual asymmetry
  • spine upright and balanced

Orientation:

  • body rotated to a controlled three-quarter angle appropriate for the requested view
  • shoulders and hips aligned consistently
  • no twisting between upper and lower body

Arms:

  • arms relaxed at sides
  • slight natural gap from torso
  • no expressive placement
  • no forward or backward swing
  • hands neutral and relaxed

Legs:

  • legs straight and evenly weighted
  • feet placed naturally and stably for a controlled three-quarter stance
  • no staggered stance
  • no bend or asymmetrical loading

Important:

  • reconstruct a clean, standardized neutral three-quarter stance
  • prioritize technical consistency over natural pose variation

docs.title: Reconstruction
docs.text:
Reconstruction process (critical):

Step 1 — Internal reconstruction:

Reconstruct the character as a neutral, fully symmetrical mannequin using the described body proportions.

  • use the reference image ONLY to extract proportions and mass distribution
  • do NOT copy the pose, stance, or silhouette from the reference
  • build a clean, upright, evenly balanced standing figure
  • ensure hips are level and weight is evenly distributed
  • ensure limbs are symmetrically placed and clearly readable

This reconstruction must be treated as a NEW pose, not derived from the reference image.

Step 2 — Silhouette rendering:

After reconstructing the neutral mannequin, render that reconstructed figure as a solid black silhouette.

  • do not refer back to the reference image during rendering
  • the silhouette must reflect the reconstructed neutral pose, not the original reference pose

docs.title: Silhouette
docs.text:
Render the character as a clean, solid black silhouette.

The silhouette must be a single unified shape with no internal detail.

Do not show:

  • anatomy lines
  • muscle definition
  • facial features
  • clothing folds
  • shading or gradients
  • lighting or highlights

The entire figure should be filled with a uniform black tone.

Edges must be crisp, clean, and clearly readable.

The silhouette should accurately reflect the character’s true body proportions and shape, including:

  • shoulder width
  • torso taper
  • waist shape
  • hip width
  • leg volume and length
  • head shape and hair silhouette

Hair must be included only as part of the outer contour.

No background elements. Plain neutral background.

docs.title: Barefoot
docs.text:
Lower body state:

  • barefoot
  • no shoes
  • no socks
  • no sandals
  • no boots
  • no footwear of any kind

Feet:

  • feet fully visible
  • feet unobstructed
  • toes and foot shape readable when visible in frame

docs.title: Minimal clothing
docs.text:
minimal standardized anatomy clothing

  • bare torso
  • fitted compression shorts
  • mid-thigh length
  • snug fit to preserve body shape readability
  • light desaturated neutral gray (consistent across all assets)
  • identical color and material across all views and assets
  • clearly distinguishable from shadows and background
  • no loose fabric
  • no additional clothing
  • no accessories
  • no props

Avoid:

  • pure black
  • very dark tones
  • bright or highly saturated colors

docs.title: Back
docs.text:
strict back-view full-body reference

Orientation:

  • body facing directly away from the camera
  • torso, hips, and legs aligned to a true back view
  • no rotation toward camera

Head alignment:

  • head aligned with torso orientation
  • no turning of the head toward camera
  • back of the head fully visible
  • no profile or three-quarter facial visibility

Silhouette requirements:

  • glute mass must be clearly visible and dominant
  • strong outward projection of the glutes must be visible from the back
  • left and right glute volumes must read as clearly separated forms
  • a subtle central separation between the glutes must be visible
  • the lower edge of the glutes must form a clear transition into the upper thighs
  • lower-body mass must read as the primary mass center
  • clear waist indentation above the glutes must be visible

Structure clarity:

  • spine alignment clearly readable
  • shoulder width and symmetry clearly defined
  • back muscle structure natural and not exaggerated
  • clear transition from lower back into glutes
  • thigh and hamstring connection clearly visible

Pose constraints:

  • neutral standing pose
  • stable and symmetrical stance
  • minimal weight shift
  • no contrapposto
  • no twisting of torso or shoulders

Constraints:

  • no flattening of glute volume
  • no merging of glutes into a flat shape
  • no upper-body dominance over lower body
  • no asymmetrical distortion unless explicitly intended
  • no flattening or smoothing of glute volume
  • no merging of left and right glutes into a single flat surface

Framing:

  • full body visible from head to feet
  • clean centered composition
  • no cropping

docs.title: Front
docs.text:
controlled front-facing full-body view

Orientation:

  • body oriented directly toward the viewer
  • torso, hips, and shoulders fully aligned to the front
  • no rotation toward or away from the viewer
  • body planes must remain frontal and symmetrical

Head alignment:

  • head facing directly forward
  • no independent rotation relative to the torso
  • both eyes fully visible and aligned
  • facial features symmetrical and centered

Pose:

  • neutral standing pose
  • weight evenly distributed across both legs
  • no visible hip shift or contrapposto
  • shoulders level and horizontally aligned
  • hips level and horizontally aligned
  • spine vertically aligned
  • posture upright but relaxed, not rigid

Silhouette requirements:

  • clean and symmetrical front silhouette
  • clear separation between arms and torso
  • legs clearly separated and readable
  • no overlap that obscures body structure
  • overall shape must be easily readable at a glance

Anatomical clarity:

  • full body proportions clearly visible from head to feet
  • major anatomical landmarks must be readable
  • no occlusion of key structural features
  • maintain consistent proportion relationships

Symmetry:

  • overall symmetry must be stable and controlled
  • minor natural asymmetry is allowed
  • avoid perfect mirrored stiffness
  • avoid visible tilt or imbalance

Constraints:

  • no rotation or twist in torso or hips
  • no dynamic pose or movement
  • no contrapposto or weight shift
  • no exaggerated posture
  • no asymmetrical stance that breaks frontal alignment

Framing:

  • full body clearly visible from head to feet
  • centered composition
  • consistent scale with other anatomy views
  • no cropping of extremities

docs.title: Side
docs.text:
strict side-view full-body reference

Orientation:

  • body aligned to a true side profile
  • torso, hips, and legs aligned on the same side axis
  • no rotation toward camera

Head alignment:

  • head aligned with torso orientation
  • no independent rotation of the head toward camera
  • face shown strictly in side profile
  • no three-quarter facial visibility

Silhouette requirements:

  • glute projection must be clearly visible and pronounced
  • lower-body mass must read as dominant
  • clear S-curve from chest → waist → glutes must be preserved

Pose constraints:

  • neutral standing pose
  • stable, balanced stance
  • minimal weight shift
  • no contrapposto
  • no twisting of torso or shoulders

Structure clarity:

  • spine alignment clearly readable
  • chest, waist, glute, and thigh transitions clearly defined
  • leg alignment clean and anatomically correct

Framing:

  • full body visible from head to feet
  • clean side silhouette
  • no cropping

docs.title: Three quarter back
docs.text:
controlled three-quarter full-body view three-quarter back orientation

Orientation:

  • body rotated to a clear three-quarter angle
  • character is turned partially away from the viewer
  • back remains the dominant visible surface
  • torso and hips turned consistently
  • body volume and structure clearly readable

Head alignment:

  • head rotation follows torso orientation
  • no excessive independent turning of the head toward camera
  • face may be only slightly visible and must remain consistent with body angle
  • avoid frontal face orientation when body is angled away

Silhouette requirements:

  • glute projection must be clearly visible
  • lower-body mass must read as dominant
  • clear structural flow from torso to waist to glutes must remain readable

Constraints:

  • do not present the torso as facing the viewer
  • avoid clear frontal chest visibility
  • no flattening of the silhouette
  • no frontal collapse of glute volume
  • no over-rotation that hides lower-body structure
  • no mismatch between head direction and torso direction

Framing:

  • full body clearly visible from head to feet
  • stable, controlled stance
  • no exaggerated twist
  • no dynamic contrapposto

docs.title: Three quarter front
docs.text:
• three-quarter front view
  • torso rotated partially toward the viewer
  • chest and front of body clearly visible
  • face partially visible (3/4 angle)
  • both eyes visible or nearly visible

docs.title: Standardized
docs.text:
Framing priority:

  • this is a face-focused reference image
  • the frame must be tightly centered on the head
  • the head must occupy the majority of the image
  • portrait canvas must not cause the framing to zoom out

Framing: standardized face reference framing

  • head centered horizontally
  • head occupies most of the frame height
  • small consistent margin above the hair
  • chin fully visible with a slightly larger lower margin
  • upper shoulders slightly visible at the bottom
  • eyes positioned slightly above center
  • framing must remain stable across face reference views

Vertical framing control:

  • the lower boundary of the frame must remain close to the base of the neck and upper shoulders
  • do not extend the frame to include the chest or torso
  • portrait canvas must not increase visible body area

Constraints:

  • no full-body framing
  • no zoomed-out portrait composition
  • no fashion-style crop variation
  • no additional empty space around the subject beyond clean reference margins

docs.title: Front
docs.text:
strict front-facing head reference

Orientation:

  • head facing directly forward
  • no rotation to either side
  • no tilt
  • no upward or downward angle

Facial visibility:

  • both eyes fully visible
  • both eyebrows fully visible
  • nose and mouth centered
  • facial features symmetrical in view

Gaze:

  • eyes directed straight toward the camera
  • pupils centered relative to eye shape
  • no lateral gaze shift

Head alignment:

  • neck aligned naturally under the head
  • no turned or twisted head position
  • no off-axis portrait pose

Constraints:

  • no three-quarter facial angle
  • no profile bias
  • no dramatic expression

Framing constraint:

  • full body must not be visible
  • image must not include legs or full torso

docs.title: Side
docs.text:
strict side-profile face reference

Orientation:

  • head rotated to a true side profile
  • no turn toward camera
  • no near-three-quarter angle
  • no tilt
  • no upward or downward angle

Head alignment:

  • head and neck aligned naturally
  • profile angle must remain clean and anatomically continuous
  • no independent twisting of the head relative to the neck
  • no off-axis portrait pose

Facial visibility:

  • only one eye visible
  • nose bridge, nose tip, lips, chin, jawline, and forehead profile clearly readable
  • ear fully visible and naturally placed
  • profile silhouette must be clean and uninterrupted

Identity requirements:

  • preserve exact facial identity from the front and three-quarter references
  • preserve forehead shape, nose shape, lip profile, chin shape, and jawline depth
  • preserve facial proportions under profile rotation
  • avoid beautification or reinterpretation of features

Constraints:

  • no dramatic expression
  • no portrait-glamour pose
  • no turn back toward camera
  • no mismatch between face angle and neck connection

docs.title: Three quarter
docs.text:
controlled three-quarter face reference

Orientation:

  • head rotated to a clear three-quarter angle
  • angle must be strong enough to show facial volume clearly
  • angle must not drift into near-front view
  • angle must not drift into side profile

Head alignment:

  • head and neck must rotate together as a single unit
  • the angle of the jaw, neck, and collar alignment must match
  • no independent rotation of the head relative to the torso
  • the connection between jaw and neck must appear anatomically continuous
  • no off-axis fashion pose
  • no tilted or thrown-back head position

Facial visibility:

  • both eyes visible
  • far eye partially reduced by perspective but still clearly readable
  • nose bridge, cheek contour, jawline, and facial planes clearly visible
  • mouth fully visible and anatomically aligned

Gaze:

  • eyes directed straight toward the camera
  • pupils centered relative to eye shape
  • no lateral gaze shift

Expression:

  • neutral facial expression
  • relaxed facial muscles
  • no smirk, tension, or stylized emotion

Identity requirements:

  • preserve exact facial identity from the front reference

docs.title: Face Anchor Sheet — v2
docs.text:
Create a clean, structured face anchor reference sheet for a character design pipeline.

This asset is used to lock the character’s facial identity across multiple angles. The result must be highly consistent, neutral, and optimized for reuse in downstream generation.

docs.title: Reference Input
docs.text:
Use the provided references with the following priority:

  1. Front view → primary identity anchor
  2. Side view → profile accuracy
  3. Three-quarter view → supporting reference only

If conflicts occur, prioritize: front > side > three-quarter

These references collectively define the canonical appearance of the character.

Strictly preserve across all views:

  • facial structure (bone structure, proportions)
  • eye shape, spacing, and alignment
  • nose shape and projection
  • mouth shape and proportions
  • jawline and chin structure
  • cheekbone structure
  • hairstyle, hairline, and volume
  • overall likeness and identity

Do NOT reinterpret, redesign, or average the face across views.

Each reference represents the same individual from a different angle and must remain consistent.

docs.title: Identity Preservation (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
• all views must depict the exact same person

  • the provided references define the canonical facial identity

  • do not reinterpret, idealize, or average facial features across views

  • do not generate a new or modified version of the face

  • preserve consistently across all views:

  • eye shape, size, and spacing
  • nose shape and projection
  • jawline shape and chin structure
  • cheekbone structure

  • overall facial proportions

  • each view must be a consistent representation of the same head from different angles

  • prioritize identity consistency over stylistic or photographic variation

  • the result should be clearly recognizable as the same individual in all panels

docs.title: Panel Assignment (STRICT)
docs.text:
The output MUST contain exactly three panels arranged horizontally:

LEFT PANEL:

  • front view
  • perfectly forward-facing
  • both eyes symmetrical

CENTER PANEL:

  • side profile
  • exact 90° profile
  • only one eye visible

RIGHT PANEL:

  • three-quarter view (~45°)
  • both eyes visible
  • far eye partially occluded

Do NOT change the order. Do NOT merge or duplicate views. Each panel must represent a clearly distinct angle.

docs.title: Angle Separation (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
The three-quarter view MUST NOT approach a full profile.

  • clear visibility of both eyes is required
  • the nose must NOT align with the facial outline
  • the far cheek must remain visible

The side view MUST remain a strict 90° profile.

These two views must be visually distinct and not interchangeable.

docs.title: View Consistency (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
• each panel must directly reflect the provided reference views
  • do not reinterpret, redraw, or modify the face in any panel

  • do not generate a new version of the face

  • the task is to arrange consistent views of the same head, not to re-render or improve them

  • preserve the exact facial structure and appearance from the input references in each corresponding view

docs.title: Layout Constraints
docs.text:
• wide horizontal canvas (landscape orientation)
  • three evenly spaced vertical panels
  • equal panel width
  • consistent head size across panels

Do NOT:

  • stack panels vertically
  • crop panels unevenly
  • output a single image instead of a 3-panel sheet

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
Include exactly three panels:

  1. Front view (perfectly front-facing)
  2. Side view (true 90° profile)
  3. Three-quarter view (approximately 45° rotation)

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
• neutral expression
  • relaxed face
  • closed mouth
  • no exaggerated emotion

docs.title: Pose & Framing
docs.text:
• head and upper neck visible
  • minimal shoulder inclusion (do not include full torso)
  • consistent scale across all panels
  • all heads aligned to the same vertical height
  • all panels centered and evenly spaced

docs.title: Camera & Perspective
docs.text:
• orthographic or near-orthographic look (avoid strong perspective distortion)
  • consistent focal length across all panels
  • no lens distortion

docs.title: Lighting
docs.text:
• soft, neutral studio lighting
  • even illumination across the face
  • no dramatic shadows
  • no directional mood lighting

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• semi-realistic rendering
  • clean and controlled
  • minimal stylization
  • avoid painterly exaggeration
  • avoid hyper-photographic noise

The result should sit between: photographic realism and clean illustration

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• plain light neutral background
  • no gradients or textures

docs.title: Layout

  • evenly spaced panels
  • no overlap between panels

Typography:

  • neutral styling
  • no decorative fonts

  • additional design elements
  • clothing details beyond minimal neckline
  • accessories (unless essential to identity)

  • consistent proportions across all views

  • identity must match the input reference exactly

## Reference Presentation

The image must present the character in a **clean studio-style anatomy reference pose** that clearly shows the glutes and hip structure.

Requirements:

• single character only
• landscape orientation
• **rear three-quarter body view**
• camera positioned slightly behind the character
• **tight anatomical crop focused on the hip region**

The image should read as a **glute anatomy study**, not a portrait.

Framing:

• **top of frame: waist / lower back (mid-back at most)**
• **bottom of frame: just above the knees**
• **the head and shoulders must NOT be visible**

The **hips and glutes must sit at the visual center of the frame**.

Only the following anatomy should be visible:

• lower back
• waist
• hips
• glutes
• upper thighs

The pose should feel **neutral and anatomical**, not posed or stylized.

Composition prioritizes the **hip and glute region rather than the full body**.

---

orthographic reference camera
rear **three-quarter perspective**
slight natural body angle
no dramatic perspective distortion

**tight anatomical crop centered on hips and glutes**

clean professional reference lighting

---

## Styling

neutral studio background
subtle grounded shadow
clean presentation
natural realistic colors

---

## Clothing

The character should wear **minimal fitted athletic shorts or simple underwear**.

Requirements:

• snug fit that clearly shows body contours
• neutral light colors (grey, light blue, beige, soft neutral tones)
• matte fabric

Avoid:

• black fabric (too dark, hides contour)
• baggy clothing
• patterns
• logos
• accessories

The clothing must **not obscure glute shape or hip contour**.

• **landscape orientation**
• **no text**

• **no multi-panel layouts**

docs.title: Anatomy Side Reference
docs.text:
Create a clean, neutral full-body profile view anatomy reference image for a character design pipeline.

This asset defines the character’s body depth, posture, and silhouette in profile and must be highly consistent and reusable.

[CHARACTER_BLOCK]

[BODY_BLOCK]

docs.title: View (PROFILE — STRICT)
docs.text:
• true 90-degree profile view

  • the body is viewed exactly from the side

  • no rotation toward or away from the viewer

  • no three-quarter angle

  • only one side of the body visible

  • the far side of the body must not be visible

docs.title: Pose (PROFILE — NEUTRAL)
docs.text:
• neutral anatomical standing pose
  • upright posture with no lean or tilt
  • shoulders and hips level and aligned
  • legs straight, hip-width apart, weight evenly distributed
  • arms hanging vertically with elbows fully extended
  • upper arms slightly separated from the torso with a consistent gap
  • hands slightly away from thighs, palms facing inward
  • fingers extended and relaxed
  • perfect left-right symmetry
  • identical pose across all views, only rotated in space

docs.title: Posture & Alignment (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
• head aligned vertically over the torso

  • ear aligned approximately over the shoulder in profile

  • spine in a natural neutral alignment

  • no forward head posture

  • no exaggerated arch in the lower back

  • pelvis in a neutral position (not tilted forward or backward)

  • knees fully extended (not bent)

  • abdomen relaxed (not flexed or held in)

docs.title: Structure & Proportions (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
• preserve the character’s exact body proportions and physical traits

  • maintain:

  • chest depth
  • abdominal projection
  • glute projection
  • back curvature
  • leg shape and thickness

  • arm thickness and length

  • preserve the natural distribution of:

  • muscle mass
  • body fat

  • softness or definition

  • do not idealize or standardize the body

  • do not increase muscle definition or reduce body fat

  • if the character has soft features, preserve softness exactly

  • if the character has asymmetry, preserve asymmetry

  • if the character has non-athletic proportions, preserve them exactly

docs.title: Silhouette Clarity (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
• the body outline must be clean and clearly readable in profile

  • the contour of:

  • chest
  • abdomen
  • glutes
  • thighs must be clearly distinguishable

docs.title: Identity Preservation
docs.text: [IDENTITY_PRESERVATION_BLOCK]

docs.title: Clothing (STANDARDIZED — FILTER SAFE)
docs.text:
• bare torso (no shirt)

  • fitted compression shorts

  • mid-thigh length
  • snug fit to clearly show body shape

  • no folds, no loose fabric

  • shorts must be in a light to mid-gray or desaturated blue or green

  • the color must be clearly visible (not black or very dark)

  • the shorts must remain clearly distinguishable from shadows and background

  • no additional clothing, accessories, or props

docs.title: Framing (STANDARDIZED)
docs.text:
• portrait image (2:3 aspect ratio)

  • full body visible from head to feet

  • no cropping of head or feet

  • character centered horizontally

  • small margin above the head

  • small margin below the feet

  • consistent scale across all anatomy panels

docs.title: Rendering (NEUTRAL)
docs.text:
• soft, even lighting

  • no strong shadows

  • plain, neutral background

  • natural skin tones

  • no stylization or painterly effects

[PANEL_OUTPUT_REQUIREMENTS]

docs.title: Ultimate Character Sheet (UCS)
docs.text:
The UCS combines the most important character reference panels into a single sheet.

Panels typically include:

  • front face
  • three-quarter face
  • profile face
  • body front
  • body side
  • silhouette
  • expression
  • dynamic pose

The UCS acts as the primary identity reference for later prompt generation.

When generating the UCS:

  1. Use the established reference sheets.
  2. Maintain consistent scale across panels.
  3. Ensure all panels clearly depict the same character.

Recommended generation order:

  1. Face panels
  2. Body panels
  3. Silhouette
  4. Expression
  5. Dynamic pose

Light stubble adds texture to his appearance, reinforcing a mature, grounded look. docs.title: Connor
docs.text:
Connor is a slim young man with a soft athletic build and a gentle, approachable presence. His physique is lightly trained, with a natural runner’s silhouette that emphasizes the lower body—his thighs and glutes are subtly more developed than his upper body, while his shoulders and torso remain lighter and less defined. This creates a soft, slightly inward silhouette that reads as relaxed and non-threatening rather than physically assertive.

His face is youthful and soft-featured, with a rounded structure, blue-grey eyes, and short medium-brown hair with a natural, slightly tousled texture. Subtle freckles across his nose and cheeks enhance his boyish appearance. Connor’s overall presence is warm, calm, and slightly shy, with an occasional absentminded quality that makes him feel gentle and emotionally open.

---

  • Height: 175 cm / 5'9"
  • Build: runner build
  • Silhouette: leg dominant
  • Face: soft round and soft jawline
  • Hair: short medium-brown hair with soft natural texture and slight curl
  • Eyes: blue-grey eyes with a gentle, slightly absentminded expression
  • Style: ['domestic soft'] and romantic
  • Palette: beige and light blue
  • Materials: cotton and linen
  • Expression: soft neutral and gentle
  • Movement: relaxed natural
  • Presence: compact presence

  • Style: rugged utilitarian and streetwear
  • Palette: black and dark grey

docs.title: Characters Overview
docs.text:
The library/10_CHARACTERS/ directory contains the full reference pipeline for each individual character.

Each character folder stores:

  • conceptual profile information
  • generated reference sheets
  • style anchors
  • motion and scene references
  • source references used to build the character

This structure is designed so that each character can be rebuilt, maintained, and reused consistently across many AI image generations.

docs.title: Character Folder Philosophy
docs.text:
Each character is treated as a self-contained reference package.

A complete character folder should contain:

  1. Profile data Human-readable and machine-readable information about the character.

  2. Identity anchors Face, anatomy, body, and UCS references that define the character visually.

  3. Style anchors Signature outfit, design language, and wardrobe sheets.

  4. Motion and scene anchors Pose sheets, motion sheets, interaction references, and scene anchors.

  5. Source references Original inspiration or source images used to build the character.

docs.title: Character Folder Structure
docs.text:
A typical character folder contains the following subfolders:

  • 00_PROFILE
  • 01_FACE
  • 02_HAIR
  • 03_ANATOMY
  • 04_PROPORTIONS
  • 05_MUSCLE
  • 06_BODY
  • 07_SILHOUETTE
  • 08_TURNAROUND
  • 09_EXPRESSIONS
  • 10_HANDS
  • 11_UCS
  • 12_SIGNATURE_OUTFIT
  • 13_DESIGN_LANGUAGE
  • 14_WARDROBE
  • 15_POSES
  • 16_MOTION
  • 17_SCALE
  • 18_SCENES
  • 19_PROPS
  • 20_GALLERY
  • IDENTITY_PACK
  • SOURCE_REFERENCES

See the library folder structure documentation for a more detailed explanation of each folder.

docs.title: The Most Important Character Files
docs.text:
The most important files for a character are usually:

  • Face Anchor Sheet
  • Anatomy Sheet
  • Body Anchor Sheet
  • Ultimate Character Sheet
  • Signature Outfit Sheet

Together, these form the character’s core identity pack.

docs.title: The Profile Folder
docs.text:
The 00_PROFILE folder contains the conceptual definition of the character.

Typical files include:

  • metadata.yaml — structured character metadata
  • character_summary.md — human-readable overview
  • prompt_blocks.md — reusable character-specific prompt fragments

These files define the character in text form before or alongside the image-based references.

docs.title: Character Lifecycle
docs.text:
A new character is usually created in this order:

  1. Create the character folder structure
  2. Fill out the 00_PROFILE files
  3. Generate face identity references
  4. Generate anatomy and body structure anchors
  5. Generate the Ultimate Character Sheet
  6. Introduce style through the signature outfit and design language sheets
  7. Expand into poses, wardrobe, motion, and scene use

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
The goal of the character system is to make each character:

  • easy to understand
  • easy to regenerate
  • easy to use in prompts
  • resistant to visual drift

docs.title: Character Templates
docs.text:
This page explains how to create and organize individual characters in the reference library.

Character folders represent the core unit of the library. Each character stores their profile information, generated reference sheets, identity packs, and source references.

The purpose of the character template system is to ensure that all characters:

  • follow the same folder structure
  • use the same profile file schema
  • move through the same reference pipeline
  • remain easy to browse in the MkDocs frontend

docs.title: Character Page Layout
docs.text:
Character pages in the MkDocs site serve as visual reference hubs for browsing a character’s generated sheets.

These pages are separate from the character asset folders and are located in:

docs/characters/

Example:

docs/characters/lucien.md

Each character page aggregates thumbnail previews of the character’s reference sheets and links to the full-size images stored in:

docs/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/

A reusable page template is provided here:

docs/characters/character-page-template.md

When creating a new character page:

  1. copy the template
  2. rename it to the character name
  3. replace placeholder paths
  4. add gallery snippets or thumbnails for the character’s available sheets

These pages are optimized for visual browsing and prompt construction, rather than for template storage.

docs.title: Character Folder Structure
docs.text:
Characters are stored in:

docs/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/

Each character has its own folder.

Example:

10_CHARACTERS/
  LUCIEN/

Inside that folder the structure is:

LUCIEN/
  00_PROFILE
  01_FACE
  02_HAIR
  03_ANATOMY
  04_PROPORTIONS
  05_MUSCLE
  06_BODY
  07_SILHOUETTE
  08_TURNAROUND
  09_EXPRESSIONS
  10_HANDS
  11_UCS
  12_SIGNATURE_OUTFIT
  13_DESIGN_LANGUAGE
  14_WARDROBE
  15_POSES
  16_MOTION
  17_SCALE
  18_SCENES
  19_PROPS

  IDENTITY_PACK
  SOURCE_REFERENCES

Each numbered folder corresponds to a stage in the character generation pipeline.

docs.title: Creating a New Character
docs.text:
To create a new character:

  1. copy the character scaffolding folder:
scaffolding/character/
  1. rename it to the character name
  2. place it inside:
docs/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/
  1. fill out the files in 00_PROFILE
  2. begin generating the character’s reference sheets following the pipeline

This is preferred over copying an existing character folder and deleting old assets.

docs.title: 00_PROFILE
docs.text:
The 00_PROFILE folder contains the conceptual definition of the character.

00_PROFILE/
  metadata.yaml
  character_summary.md
  prompt_blocks.md
  identity_guardrails.md

These files define the character before reference sheets are generated.

docs.title: metadata.yaml
docs.text:
Structured metadata describing the character.

Typical contents include:

  • core identity summary
  • physical information
  • facial information
  • style information
  • expression and movement traits
  • identity rules
  • reference file links
  • pipeline progress

This file is used for:

  • structured character data
  • indexing
  • future automation
  • library maintenance

The canonical template lives in:

scaffolding/character/00_PROFILE/metadata.yaml

docs.title: character_summary.md
docs.text:
Human-readable overview of the character.

This file typically includes:

  • core identity
  • short and full visual identity descriptions
  • silhouette summary
  • style identity
  • body language
  • expression profile
  • identity preservation rules
  • core reference sheets

This file acts as a condensed character reference document.

The canonical template lives in:

scaffolding/character/00_PROFILE/character_summary.md

docs.title: prompt_blocks.md
docs.text:
Reusable prompt fragments describing the character.

Typical blocks include:

  • Character Block
  • Identity Block (Short)
  • Identity Block (Extended)
  • Face Block
  • Body Block
  • Style Block
  • Movement Block
  • Expression Block
  • Wardrobe Description Block
  • Anti-Drift Rules
  • Short Prompt Description
  • Full Prompt Description

These blocks are used when building prompts for reference generation and later scenes.

The canonical template lives in:

scaffolding/character/00_PROFILE/prompt_blocks.md

docs.title: identity_guardrails.md
docs.text:
Defines non-negotiable identity constraints for the character.

This file is used when:

  • generating new reference sheets
  • creating outfits or scenes
  • troubleshooting generator drift
  • reviewing whether an image still reads as the same character

Typical contents include:

  • core identity locks
  • silhouette guardrails
  • facial guardrails
  • style guardrails
  • expression guardrails
  • movement guardrails
  • known generator drift risks
  • reference hierarchy
  • identity test checklist

This file should be concise but clear. Some characters may need only a short version, while others benefit from more detailed guardrails.

The canonical template lives in:

scaffolding/character/00_PROFILE/identity_guardrails.md

docs.title: Identity Pack
docs.text:
IDENTITY_PACK/

This folder stores the most important identity-stabilizing references for the character.

Examples:

  • face anchors
  • body anchors
  • turnaround sheets
  • signature outfit references

These are the assets most likely to be attached during prompt generation.

docs.title: Source References
docs.text:
SOURCE_REFERENCES/

This folder stores external references and non-canonical source material.

Examples:

SOURCE_REFERENCES/
  legacy_pipeline/
  inspiration/
  raw/

This may include:

  • cropped legacy images
  • older pipeline outputs
  • inspiration images
  • raw generation outputs

These assets do not need to follow the current sheet layout to remain useful.

docs.title: Character Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The individual character pipeline focuses on defining the character’s own identity and structure.

Typical stages include:

Stage Purpose Face establish facial identity Hair define hairstyle consistency Anatomy define body construction Body / Silhouette / Turnaround stabilize full-body identity Expression / Hands define expressive range UCS consolidate identity into one master sheet Outfit / Design Language define style and wardrobe Poses / Motion / Scale / Scenes expand character usage

docs.title: Minimum Character Setup
docs.text:
Before starting image generation, each character should have:

  • a character folder created from scaffolding
  • completed metadata.yaml
  • completed character_summary.md
  • completed prompt_blocks.md
  • an initial identity_guardrails.md

Once these are in place, the visual reference pipeline can begin.

docs.title: Recommended Workflow
docs.text:
1. create the character folder from scaffolding
  2. fill in 00_PROFILE
  3. generate face references
  4. generate anatomy references
  5. generate body identity sheets
  6. generate UCS
  7. generate signature outfit and design language
  8. expand into wardrobe, poses, motion, scale, scenes, and props

docs.title: Relationship to Other Template Pages
docs.text:
This page documents individual character templates.

Related pages:

  • docs/pairs/templates.md for character pairs
  • docs/groups/templates.md for groups
  • docs/prompts/templates-index.md for prompt template browsing

Character templates define the individual unit of the library. Pairs and groups define relationship-focused units built on top of those individual characters.

docs.title: Controlled Vocabulary
docs.text:
This page defines standardized values used in character metadata.

The purpose of this vocabulary is to keep character descriptions consistent across:

  • metadata files
  • summary pages
  • prompt blocks
  • gallery pages
  • future automation

Use these values whenever possible instead of inventing new terms for each character.

docs.title: Build Categories
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.build_category.

Value Description soft_slender slender frame with soft musculature and refined proportions narrow_slender slender build with a narrow frame and delicate body structure elongated_slender slender build with visibly long limbs and elongated proportions light_athletic lightly toned body with visible fitness but little bulk runner_build athletic build with lower-body emphasis and lean overall mass lower_athletic athletic build with noticeable lower-body dominance balanced_athletic proportional athletic build with moderate tone and balanced mass athletic_muscular clearly defined muscular physique without extreme bulk heavy_muscular thick muscular body with strong mass and visible density power_build very broad and powerful build with heavy upper-body presence broad_heavy broad frame with substantial overall body mass thick_set dense body build with strong torso mass and compact power large_frame naturally large skeletal frame regardless of muscle level soft_heavy body with noticeable softness and weight without strong muscular structure; mass reads as natural body fat rather than muscle density

docs.title: Silhouette Anchor
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.silhouette_anchor.

Value Description runner_silhouette lean athletic silhouette with strong lower-body emphasis and light upper-body mass power_athlete broad, muscular athletic silhouette with dominant shoulders and chest elongated_slender slender silhouette defined by long limbs and extended vertical proportions power_frame extremely broad, dense, muscular silhouette defined by heavy upper-body mass glute_slender slender silhouette where the lower body is visually defined by rounded glutes relative to a narrow waist and slim upper body glute_heavy silhouette strongly defined by prominent glutes relative to waist and thighs, creating a visually rear-weighted lower-body shape hip_dominant_soft silhouette defined by fuller hips, glutes, and thighs with soft contours, producing a lower-body-weighted shape rather than a shoulder-dominant frame

docs.title: Silhouette Emphasis
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.silhouette_emphasis.

Value Description balanced silhouette mass appears evenly distributed across the body with no strongly dominant region shoulders shoulder width strongly defines the silhouette relative to hips and torso chest chest mass or structure visually defines the upper-body silhouette upper_body shoulders, chest, and upper torso dominate the silhouette relative to hips and legs torso the midsection or abdominal area visually defines the body mass distribution waist a narrow waist strongly defines the silhouette by creating a visible taper between shoulders and hips hips hip width strongly defines the silhouette relative to shoulders glutes rounded glutes visually define the silhouette relative to waist and thighs thighs thigh mass or width visually defines the lower-body silhouette hips_glutes hips and glutes together define the lower-body silhouette glutes_thighs glutes and thighs form the primary mass and shape of the silhouette hips_glutes_thighs hips, glutes, and thighs together create the dominant silhouette mass relative to the upper body legs overall leg length or leg mass defines the silhouette relative to the torso

docs.title: Silhouette Keywords
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.silhouette_keywords.

Value Description compact tight, condensed body proportions tall visually tall vertical silhouette broad wide shoulder silhouette imposing large presence with strong physical scale agile light, athletic movement-oriented silhouette leg_dominant lower body visually emphasized upper_dominant upper body visually emphasized glute_emphasis silhouette visually defined by prominent rounded glutes relative to waist and thighs heavy_set dense mass-focused silhouette massive extreme muscular scale and physical mass dominate silhouette

docs.title: Shoulder Profiles
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.shoulder_profile.

Value Description narrow_shoulders visibly narrow shoulder width moderate_shoulders balanced shoulder width broad_shoulders visibly wide shoulder width heavy_shoulders thick, mass-heavy shoulder construction

docs.title: Torso Profiles
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.torso_profile.

Value Description slim_torso narrow torso with low bulk soft_torso lightly built torso with soft definition athletic_torso toned torso with visible definition broad_torso wide torso with strong width thick_torso dense, heavy torso mass

docs.title: Limb Profiles
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.limb_profile.

Value Description delicate_limbs slim, fine-boned limb structure slender_limbs narrow limbs with understated mass long_limbs visibly elongated limbs athletic_limbs toned limbs with moderate definition thick_limbs limbs with strong width and density

docs.title: Posture Profiles
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.posture_profile.

Value Description upright_controlled straight, composed posture with control relaxed_neutral natural, relaxed standing posture grounded_stable heavy, planted posture with strong balance soft_reserved slightly inward, gentle posture confident_open open posture with visible confidence

docs.title: Body Fat Ranges

Value Description lean visible definition athletic clearly trained physique soft_average healthy but untrained body soft_heavy noticeable softness

docs.title: Height Visual Categories
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.height_visual_category.

Value Description short visibly below average height; character reads clearly shorter than most others (approx. under ~170 cm / 5'7") medium average or typical height; character reads neither short nor tall in most scenes (approx. ~170–180 cm / 5'7"–5'11") tall clearly above average height; character reads noticeably taller than many others (approx. ~180–190 cm / 5'11"–6'3") imposing extremely tall or physically dominant height presence; character towers over others visually (approx. over ~190 cm / 6'3")

docs.title: Body Softness Distributions
docs.text:
Use these values for physical.body_softness_distribution.

Value Description balanced body softness distributed evenly across torso and limbs lower_body softness concentrated in hips, glutes, and thighs rather than stomach or chest torso softness concentrated in stomach and waist area upper_body softness concentrated in chest, shoulders, and arms glute_dominant softness concentrated specifically in glutes and hips, creating a rounded lower-body silhouette firm_all musculature appears firm and defined across the entire body with minimal softness soft_lower_body lower body appears slightly softer or fuller compared to upper body soft_upper_body upper body carries slightly more softness than the lower body balanced_softness moderate softness distributed evenly without strong regional emphasis

docs.title: Frame Proportions

docs.text:

  • dangerous_romance — intimate dynamic defined by tension between softness and danger

docs.title: Reference Library Folder Structure
docs.text:
The reference library is stored inside:

docs/assets/library/

This folder contains all generated assets, reference images, and prompt templates used in the character generation pipeline.

Unlike many documentation projects, this system intentionally stores the full asset library directly inside docs/assets/ so that all files are immediately accessible through the MkDocs site.

Documentation explaining how the system works lives in:

docs/

The docs/assets/library/ folder stores the actual reference images and generation resources.

docs.title: Top-Level Library Structure
docs.text:
docs/assets/library/

10_CHARACTERS
20_CHARACTER_PAIRS
30_CHARACTER_GROUPS
40_ENVIRONMENTS
50_PROMPT_TEMPLATES
60_INSPIRATION

docs.title: 10_CHARACTERS
docs.text:
Contains the full reference pipeline for each individual character.

Each character receives its own folder with all reference sheets generated through the pipeline.

Example:

10_CHARACTERS/
├── LUCIEN/
├── RAGNAR/
└── JONAH/

Each character folder contains anatomy references, style sheets, pose sheets, and other generated resources.

docs.title: 20_CHARACTER_PAIRS
docs.text:
Contains resources for two-character relationships.

This includes reference sheets used when two characters frequently appear together.

Typical contents:

  • height comparison sheets
  • interaction anchors
  • couple pose sheets
  • scene anchors involving both characters

Example:

20_CHARACTER_PAIRS/
├── LUCIEN__RAGNAR/
└── JASPER__BLAKE/

docs.title: 30_CHARACTER_GROUPS
docs.text:
Contains resources for groups of three or more characters.

Useful for teams, families, ensembles, or story casts.

Typical contents:

  • group lineup sheets
  • group pose sheets
  • interaction scenes
  • group scene anchors

Example:

30_CHARACTER_GROUPS/
├── WITCH_COVEN/
└── GYM_CREW/

docs.title: 40_ENVIRONMENTS
docs.text:
Contains reference sheets for locations and environments where characters appear.

These act as scene anchors to keep locations visually consistent.

Typical environment sheets include:

  • room layouts
  • lighting references
  • architectural details
  • environmental mood references

Example environments:

40_ENVIRONMENTS/

LUCIEN_APARTMENT/
RITUAL_CHAMBER/
GYM_INTERIOR/
CITY_STREET/

Environment anchors are often attached to prompts when generating scene images.

docs.title: 50_PROMPT_TEMPLATES
docs.text:
Contains reusable prompt templates used throughout the pipeline.

Templates are organized by generation stage.

Example:

50_PROMPT_TEMPLATES/

00_MASTER_BLOCKS
01_FACE_ANCHORS
03_ANATOMY
11_UCS

Each template should include reusable placeholder blocks such as:

[CHARACTER BLOCK]
[GLOBAL STYLE BLOCK]

These allow prompts to be reused across multiple characters.

docs.title: 60_INSPIRATION
docs.text:
Contains reference images used as design inspiration.

These are not generated assets, but visual references that influence character design.

Examples include:

  • fashion references
  • architecture references
  • lighting references
  • pose inspiration
  • color palette inspiration

Example structure:

60_INSPIRATION/

FASHION/
LIGHTING/
POSES/
COLOR_PALETTES/
ARCHITECTURE/

These images are sometimes attached to prompts to guide visual style.

docs.title: Character Folder Structure
docs.text:
Each character folder contains the complete reference pipeline for that character.

Example:

10_CHARACTERS/
└── LUCIEN/

Inside each character folder:

[CHARACTER_NAME]/
├── 00_SOURCE_REFERENCES/
│   ├── face/

docs.title: Gallery Snippet Conventions
docs.text:
This page defines the standard used for gallery snippet files in the character reference library.

Gallery snippets are used to keep character pages short, consistent, and easier to maintain.

They contain the HTML for thumbnail galleries and are included into character pages using pymdownx.snippets.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Use gallery snippets when a character page needs to display one or more reference images in a reusable gallery block.

This keeps:

  • character pages shorter
  • gallery markup centralized
  • updates easier when image filenames or versions change
  • section structure consistent across characters

docs.title: Snippet Location
docs.text:
All gallery snippets should be stored in:

docs/snippets/galleries/

Example:

docs/snippets/galleries/lucien-face.md
docs/snippets/galleries/lucien-body.md
docs/snippets/galleries/lucien-anatomy.md

docs.title: Include Syntax
docs.text:
Character pages include gallery snippets using this syntax:

<div class="character-gallery">

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_front_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_front_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_profile_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_profile_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_three_quarter_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_three_quarter_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

</div>

This works because mkdocs.yml configures pymdownx.snippets with:

pymdownx.snippets:
  base_path:
    - docs

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text:
Gallery snippet filenames should use this structure:

[character-slug]-[section-name].md

Examples:

lucien-core-identity.md
lucien-face.md
lucien-hair.md
lucien-anatomy.md
lucien-body.md
lucien-expression-gesture.md

Use lowercase kebab-case for the full filename.

docs.title: Standard Section Names
docs.text: Use these section names wherever possible.

docs.title: Core sections
docs.text:
core-identity
face
hair
anatomy
body
expression-gesture

docs.title: Advanced sections
docs.text:
ucs
signature-outfit
design-language
wardrobe
poses
motion
scale
scenes
props

These names should match the logical page sections, not necessarily the raw folder names.

docs.title: What Belongs in a Snippet
docs.text:
A gallery snippet should contain only the gallery HTML block.

Example:

<div class="character-gallery">
  <a
    href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png"
    target="_blank"
  >
    <img
      src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png"
      alt="Lucien face anchor"
    />
  </a>
</div>

A snippet should not contain:

  • page headings
  • explanatory paragraphs
  • markdown lists
  • horizontal rules
  • unrelated notes

The snippet should only contain the visual gallery markup.

docs.title: 1. Use only HTML inside gallery snippets
docs.text:
Gallery snippets should contain only:

  • <div>
  • <a>
  • <img>

Do not mix markdown headings or markdown formatting into the snippet file.

This keeps rendering stable inside MkDocs.

docs.title: 2. Use the shared gallery wrapper
docs.text:
Every gallery snippet should use:

<div class="character-gallery"></div>

This ensures the shared CSS applies consistently.

docs.title: 3. Use /assets/... paths, not /docs/assets/...
docs.text:
Correct:

/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png

Incorrect:

/docs/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png

MkDocs serves the contents of docs/ at the site root, so runtime asset paths must begin with /assets/.

docs.title: 4. Always include descriptive alt text
docs.text:
Every image must include useful alt text.

Good:

alt="Lucien face anchor"
alt="Lucien anatomy front"
alt="Lucien expression sheet"

Avoid vague values like:

alt="image"
alt="reference"

docs.title: 5. Keep one snippet per page section
docs.text:
Each major character page section should normally have its own snippet file.

Example:

  • lucien-face.md
  • lucien-anatomy.md
  • lucien-body.md

Do not combine unrelated sections into one large snippet unless there is a clear reason.

docs.title: 6. Update snippets when image versions change
docs.text:
If an asset changes from:

lucien_face_anchor_v1.png

to:

lucien_face_anchor_v2.png

update the snippet file so the character page continues to point to the newest intended version.

This is one of the main maintenance benefits of using snippets.

docs.title: Character Page Responsibilities
docs.text:
The character page should contain:

  • headings
  • short descriptive section text
  • include lines for the gallery snippets
  • prompting notes
  • navigation

The character page should not contain large repeated image blocks directly unless there is a strong reason.

Example:

## Face References

These references define facial identity, angle consistency, and portrait fidelity.

<div class="character-gallery">

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_face_anchor_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_front_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_front_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_profile_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_profile_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

  <a href="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_three_quarter_face_v1.png" target="_blank">
    <img src="/assets/library/10_CHARACTERS/LUCIEN/01_FACE/lucien_three_quarter_face_v1.png" alt="">
  </a>

</div>

docs.title: Recommended Character Page Pattern
docs.text:
Use this structure for character pages where available:

Overview
Quick Navigation
Core Identity
Face References
Hair References
Anatomy
Body / Proportions
Expression and Gesture
Advanced Reference Sets
Prompting Notes

Not every character needs every section immediately, but the naming and layout should remain as consistent as possible.

docs.title: Example Snippet Set
docs.text:
A typical character with current core coverage may have:

docs/snippets/galleries/
  lucien-core-identity.md
  lucien-face.md
  lucien-hair.md
  lucien-anatomy.md
  lucien-body.md
  lucien-expression-gesture.md

As the library expands, additional snippets may be added:

lucien-ucs.md
lucien-signature-outfit.md
lucien-design-language.md
lucien-wardrobe.md
lucien-poses.md
lucien-motion.md
lucien-scale.md
lucien-scenes.md
lucien-props.md

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Gallery snippets are the standard way to render reference galleries in character pages.

Use them to keep pages:

  • clean
  • modular
  • maintainable
  • visually consistent

When in doubt:

  • keep headings in the character page
  • keep gallery HTML in the snippet
  • keep asset paths rooted at /assets/
  • keep filenames predictable

docs.text:

docs.title: Output Format Standards
docs.text:
These standards define the intended aspect ratio family for each resource type.

Resource Type Format Family Notes Front face reference square centered head reference Three-quarter face reference square centered head reference Profile face reference square centered head reference Face anchor sheet portrait multi-panel identity sheet Hair reference sheet portrait multi-panel structure sheet Anatomy sheet portrait full-body multi-panel sheet Body anchor sheet portrait full-body identity sheet Silhouette sheet portrait multi-panel outline sheet Turnaround sheet landscape multi-angle layout Expression sheet portrait multi-panel facial acting sheet Hand sheet portrait multi-panel hand references UCS portrait gallery-friendly master sheet Signature outfit sheet portrait consistent wardrobe display Wardrobe master sheet landscape multiple outfits in one sheet

docs.title: Pair Templates
docs.text:
This page explains how to create and organize character pairs in the reference library.

Character pairs represent two characters that frequently appear together and have a recognizable visual relationship.

Examples:

  • romantic pairs
  • rivals
  • siblings
  • mentor/student
  • teammates

Pairs focus on visual dynamics between characters, not just their individual identities.

docs.title: Pair Folder Structure
docs.text:
Pairs are stored in:

docs/assets/library/20_CHARACTER_PAIRS/

Each pair has its own folder.

Example:

20_CHARACTER_PAIRS/
  BLAKE_JASPER/

Inside that folder the structure is:

BLAKE_JASPER/
  00_PROFILE/
  01_SCALE/
  02_DYNAMICS/
  03_WARDROBE/
  04_SCENES/

  IDENTITY_PACK/
  SOURCE_REFERENCES/

Unlike individual characters, pair folders focus on relationship assets rather than individual anatomy or wardrobe.

docs.title: Pair Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The pair pipeline focuses on the visual relationship between two characters.

Typical stages include:

Stage Purpose Profile Define the pair identity and dynamics Scale Establish height and build relationships Dynamics Capture body language and interaction style Wardrobe Explore coordinated or contrasting outfits Scenes Anchor the pair in shared environments

docs.title: 00_PROFILE
docs.text:
The profile folder defines the identity of the pair itself.

00_PROFILE/
  metadata.yaml
  pair_summary.md
  prompt_blocks.md
  identity_guardrails.md

docs.title: metadata.yaml
docs.text:
Structured metadata describing the pair.

Contains:

  • member characters
  • dynamic keywords
  • style relationship
  • height relationship
  • visual contrast notes

Used for:

  • library indexing
  • prompt generation
  • documentation.

docs.title: pair_summary.md
docs.text:
Human-readable overview of the pair.

Includes:

  • core identity description
  • dynamic summary
  • height and scale relationship
  • styling relationship
  • identity preservation notes.

This document explains how the pair should visually read together.

docs.title: prompt_blocks.md
docs.text:
Reusable prompt fragments describing the pair.

Typical blocks include:

  • pair character block
  • extended identity block
  • scale block
  • dynamic block
  • style relationship block

These blocks can be copied directly into prompts.

docs.title: identity_guardrails.md
docs.text:
Defines non-negotiable visual rules for the pair.

This file prevents identity drift when generating images.

Typical sections include:

  • core pair locks
  • scale guardrails
  • identity guardrails
  • dynamic guardrails
  • style guardrails
  • known generator drift risks
  • reference hierarchy

Guardrails are used when reviewing generated images or troubleshooting identity problems.

docs.title: 01_SCALE
docs.text:
Scale sheets define relative physical relationships.

Examples:

blake_jasper_height_comparison_v1.png
blake_jasper_scale_sheet_v1.png

These sheets establish:

  • height differences
  • build contrast
  • silhouette relationships.

docs.title: 02_DYNAMICS
docs.text:

docs.title: Identity Pack
docs.text:
IDENTITY_PACK/

This folder stores curated assets used to stabilize generation:

  • face anchors
  • body anchors
  • pair interaction anchors
  • scale references.

These are the most important references when generating pair scenes.

docs.title: Source References
docs.text:
SOURCE_REFERENCES/

Stores external references and legacy assets.

Examples:

SOURCE_REFERENCES/
  inspiration/
  legacy_pipeline/
  raw/

These assets may not follow the pipeline layout but remain valuable references.

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Pair folders use uppercase member names separated by underscores.

Example:

BLAKE_JASPER

File naming convention:

blake_jasper_height_comparison_v1.png
blake_jasper_interaction_anchor_v1.png
blake_jasper_scene_anchor_v1.png

docs.title: Creating a New Pair
docs.text:
1. Copy the pair scaffolding folder:
scaffolding/pair/
  1. Rename it:
PAIR_NAME
  1. Place it inside:
docs/assets/library/20_CHARACTER_PAIRS/

  1. Fill in:

  2. metadata.yaml

  3. pair_summary.md
  4. prompt_blocks.md

  5. identity_guardrails.md

  6. Generate pair reference sheets.

docs.title: Relationship to Character Assets
docs.text:
Pair assets do not replace individual character references.

Instead they complement them.

Pair prompts should attach:

  1. pair interaction anchors
  2. pair scale sheets
  3. individual character face anchors
  4. individual body anchors

This preserves both:

  • individual character identity
  • pair dynamics.

docs.text:

  2. Hair Identity
  3. Physique Anchoring

Each stage adds a specific type of stability to the character.

docs.title: Block Placeholder Names
docs.text:
Prompt templates reference reusable blocks using standardized placeholders.

These placeholders correspond to files stored in:

assets/library/50_PROMPT_TEMPLATES/00_MASTER_BLOCKS/

Templates should always use these canonical placeholder names.

Placeholder Block File [CHARACTER_BLOCK] character-block-template.md [GLOBAL_STYLE_BLOCK] global-style-block.md [IDENTITY_PRESERVATION_BLOCK] identity-preservation-block.md [LAYOUT_BLOCK] layout-block.md [LABELS_BLOCK] labels-block.md [CAMERA_BLOCK] camera-block.md [LIGHTING_BLOCK] lighting-block.md [BACKGROUND_BLOCK] background-block.md [REFERENCE_FIDELITY_BLOCK] reference-fidelity-block.md [REFERENCE_SHEET_BLOCK_STACK] reference-sheet-block-stack.md [REFERENCE_PANEL_BLOCK_STACK] reference-panel-block-stack.md [SCENE_BLOCK_STACK] scene-block-stack.md [SQUARE_REFERENCE_FORMAT_BLOCK] square-reference-format-block.md [PORTRAIT_SHEET_FORMAT_BLOCK] portrait-sheet-format-block.md [LANDSCAPE_SHEET_FORMAT_BLOCK] landscape-sheet-format-block.md

When writing prompt templates:

  • always reference the canonical placeholder names
  • avoid inventing new block names
  • reuse the existing master blocks whenever possible
  • use block stacks when a template consistently uses the same combination of blocks
  • use format blocks to standardize aspect-ratio families across the library

This ensures prompt templates remain consistent across the pipeline.

docs.title: Prompt System Overview
docs.text:
This project uses a modular prompt system designed to reduce character drift when generating images with AI models.

The system is composed of three layers:

  1. master prompt blocks
  2. prompt recipes
  3. pipeline prompt templates

Prompt blocks contain reusable text fragments.

Prompt recipes explain how to combine blocks for different tasks.

Pipeline templates are full prompts used to generate specific reference sheets.

Prompt templates use block placeholders such as:

[GLOBAL_STYLE_BLOCK]

These blocks are defined in the master blocks folder.

When generating prompts with ChatGPT, the master block definitions must be provided so the model can resolve the placeholders.

docs.title: Prompt Recipes
docs.text:
This page explains how prompts are constructed using the modular prompt system.

Prompts are built from three components:

  1. Master Blocks Global prompt fragments used across all characters.

  2. Character Prompt Blocks Character-specific descriptions stored in each character’s prompt_blocks.md.

  3. Prompt Templates Pipeline templates stored in library/50_PROMPT_TEMPLATES/.

docs.title: Basic Prompt Structure
docs.text:
Most prompts follow this structure:

Character block

  • task description
  • style block
  • layout block
  • identity preservation rules

Example structure:

Character:
[CHARACTER_BLOCK]

Task description:
[WHAT SHOULD BE GENERATED]

[GLOBAL STYLE BLOCK]

[LAYOUT BLOCK]

[IDENTITY PRESERVATION BLOCK]
